[0] Water damage is one of those problems where a single sensor can save you a hefty repair bill, covering floors, cabinetry, and more. Leak sensors have long been one of the best-value products in the smart home category, and Shelly's newly released Flood S Gen4 makes getting started even easier. It is priced under US$30, carries Matter certification, and supports Apple Home right out of the box.

[1] HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

[2] Larger sensing surface

[3] Most leak sensors on the market use small metal probes on the bottom, meaning water has to pool in exactly the right spot to trigger an alert. Shelly's new sensor takes a different approach, featuring three large stainless-steel sensing pads on the underside of the device. The greater contact area means faster leak detection and wider coverage — precisely the reason you would place a sensor under a water heater or washing machine.

[4] The sensing pads are also sensitive enough to detect clean or low-conductivity water, such as condensate from an air conditioner. These types of leaks are typically harder to spot. With its slim profile, the Flood S Gen4 can slide under appliances, behind toilets, and beneath sinks — exactly where these sensors are best positioned.

[5] Matter/Apple Home support

[6] The Flood S Gen4 is Matter-certified and supports both Wi-Fi and Zigbee, so it works with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Once added to Apple Home, the automation possibilities expand significantly:

  • [7] The moment a leak is detected, cut power to the washing machine or dishwasher (if connected via a smart plug)
  • [8] Trigger every smart light bulb in the home
  • [9] Simple leak alert notifications on your iPhone (incredibly useful if you are out and about)

[10] Modes, alerts, and battery life

[11] In addition to phone notifications, a built-in local alarm ensures that anyone at home will hear it even if the phone is in another room. Shelly offers two operating modes — flood detection and rain detection — along with three alert settings (intense, normal, economy), letting you strike a balance between detection speed and battery life. With the included CR123A battery, battery life can reach up to two years.

[12] Summary

[13] At under US$30, you can buy three or four of these without a second thought. Place one in front of the water heater, in front of the dishwasher, under the washing machine, and beneath the kitchen sink. Matter/Apple Home support means you can receive alerts through the Home app and build Apple Home automations around it. There is a lot to appreciate about this product, and no drawbacks to be found. Trust me — leak sensors are the smartest investment in any smart home.

[14] You can pick up the Shelly Flood S Gen4 on Amazon or directly from Shelly.
